_comment: Pinned third-party runtimes bundled into dining-setup.exe.
These three are pinned as a SET, not individually. Apache's mod_php DLL and the PHP build
must come from the same Visual Studio toolset (VS16 here) or Apache will not load PHP at
all. Do not upgrade one without the other, and do not substitute a VS17 Apache while using
fetch-runtimes.ps1 copies these out of a local Laragon install by default, because that is
the combination already proven to run together on the build machine.

php.why: Thread-safe (ZTS) is required for mod_php; it is the build that ships php8apache2_4.dll. An NTS build cannot be used with mod_php.

apache.why: VS16 build, matching the PHP toolset. Registers itself as a Windows service via 'httpd -k install', so no third-party service wrapper is needed.

mysql.why: Pinned to 8.0.x. MySQL 8.4 REMOVED mysql_native_password, which the counter app's PyMySQL needs unless the cryptography package is present. dining-full.sql is also produced by this mysqldump.

vcredist.why: mysqld.exe, httpd.exe and php.exe are all VS16/VS17-toolset binaries and depend on the Visual C++ runtime DLLs. This dev machine already has them from years of other installs, which is exactly why this was missing undetected for so long: mysqld.exe crashed with exit -1073741515 (0xC0000135, STATUS_DLL_NOT_FOUND) on the first real install to a genuinely clean Windows 10/11 PC, and every artisan call after it cascaded from there. Microsoft's own aka.ms redirect always serves the latest VS 2015-2022 redistributable; the sha256 above is pinned to what fetch-runtimes.ps1 last verified, and it re-verifies on every fetch rather than trusting a cached file blindly.
